prompt: What decides how hard a password is to guess?

choices.text: how recently it was changed for a new one
choices.why: Age decides nothing about guessing.

choices.text: whether it contains a word from a dictionary
choices.why: A matter of shape, not of the arithmetic.

choices.text: its length, overwhelmingly, and its alphabet weakly
choices.why: Which is why four words beat a mangled one.

choices.text: the number of symbols and digits somebody has put into it
choices.why: That is the advice that produces short passwords.

prompt: Why is `Password@2024` weaker than its length suggests?

choices.text: the symbol in the middle is one of very few used
choices.why: Part of the shape, and not the argument.

choices.text: it has the shape people were taught to produce
choices.why: And a guessing tool tries those shapes first.

choices.text: it is too short for any alphabet to save it
choices.why: Thirteen characters would be fine if random.

choices.text: the year in it can be looked up by the attacker
choices.why: Every year is tried, and that is not the point.

prompt: What is the attack that actually takes ordinary accounts?

choices.text: somebody guessing at the login page for hours
choices.why: Rate limits make this unusual.

choices.text: an attacker reading the password from the screen
choices.why: Rare, and not what this section is about.

choices.text: a program watching what is typed on the keyboard
choices.why: It happens, and it is not the common case.

choices.text: a password reused on a site that was breached
choices.why: Nobody guesses; they try the list everywhere.

prompt: What is the real objection to a password manager, and the answer?

choices.text: it cannot be used on a phone, only on a computer
choices.why: They all work on phones.

choices.text: the company can read every password it stores
choices.why: They are encrypted behind the master password.

choices.text: one point of failure, against fifty reuses of one password
choices.why: The alternative in practice is worse, and unencrypted.

choices.text: it stops working when there is no connection
choices.why: The store is local as well.

prompt: Why is filling in a password automatically a safety feature?

choices.text: a filled password is never seen by the keyboard
choices.why: Not the argument, and not reliably true.

choices.text: the manager fills only on the address it saved it for
choices.why: A convincing copy of the page gets nothing.

choices.text: it changes the password each time it is used
choices.why: Nothing does that.

choices.text: it means the password is never typed in public
choices.why: A benefit, and a small one.

prompt: What should the answer to a security question be?

choices.text: a short answer, since it is typed under pressure
choices.why: Length is not the problem here.

choices.text: the true answer, so it can never be forgotten
choices.why: The true answer is findable.

choices.text: something invented, and stored in the manager
choices.why: The true answers are public facts about you.

choices.text: the same answer used on every site that asks
choices.why: That is reuse, one layer down.

prompt: The rule that matters is not make it complicated; it is never use it ___.
Which second factor is the weakest of the four?

choices.text: a passkey held by the phone
choices.why: The newest and the strongest.

choices.text: a code sent by SMS
choices.why: A number can be moved to somebody else's SIM.

choices.text: a physical key that plugs in
choices.why: The strongest of the traditional three.

choices.text: a code from an app on the phone
choices.why: Nothing is sent, so nothing is intercepted.

prompt: Why is an app code not interceptable?

choices.text: the phone refuses to show it to another app
choices.why: Not the mechanism.

choices.text: nothing is sent; both sides compute the same number
choices.why: From one secret and the clock.

choices.text: the code changes before anybody can use it
choices.why: Thirty seconds is enough to use one.

choices.text: the code is encrypted along the whole way to the phone
choices.why: There is no way for it to travel.

prompt: What is different about a passkey?

choices.text: it replaces the fingerprint rather than the password
choices.why: The fingerprint unlocks it.

choices.text: the site never learns a secret at all
choices.why: It replaces the password rather than adding to it.

choices.text: it works only on the device that created it
choices.why: They sync between a person's devices.

choices.text: it is a longer password held by the browser
choices.why: It is not a password.

prompt: Why do the recovery codes matter more than they look?

choices.text: losing the phone is the likeliest thing to happen
choices.why: And they are the only way back in.

choices.text: the service asks you for one of them every few months
choices.why: It does not.

choices.text: they prove to a court that the account belongs to you
choices.why: No legal role at all.

choices.text: they work as a second factor of their own
choices.why: They are the way past it, once each.

prompt: Where should a screenshot of the recovery codes NOT be?

choices.text: stored in the password manager itself
choices.why: Reasonable, if it is not behind that factor.

choices.text: written by hand on a card in a drawer
choices.why: Also right.

choices.text: printed out and kept with important papers
choices.why: Exactly where they should be.

choices.text: on the phone that holds the second factor
choices.why: A copy of the key inside the lock.

prompt: Where should the second factor go first?

choices.text: the social accounts, because they are attacked most
choices.why: They are not the lever.

choices.text: the e-mail address, because everything resets through it
choices.why: Control the mailbox and you control the rest.

choices.text: everywhere at once, so nothing is left out
choices.why: Nobody finishes that, and the order matters.

choices.text: the bank, because that is where the money is
choices.why: Second, and only second.

prompt: Why does publishing a fix make unpatched machines more exposed?

choices.text: the problem becomes public and tools follow in days
choices.why: Automated and indiscriminate.

choices.text: an unpatched machine reports its version to everybody
choices.why: Not how it works.

choices.text: the maker stops defending the old version at once
choices.why: There was no defence to stop.

choices.text: the fix tells attackers which machines are unpatched
choices.why: They scan rather than read.

prompt: What is wrong with an update that is downloaded and never applied?

choices.text: it slows the machine while it waits
choices.why: It does not.

choices.text: it prevents later updates from arriving
choices.why: They queue up fine.

choices.text: it takes up disk space until it is installed
choices.why: True and trivial.

choices.text: it is the same as no update at all
choices.why: Restart later, pressed for six weeks.

prompt: Which program matters most to keep current, and why?

choices.text: the antivirus, which is the defence itself
choices.why: Useful, and it is not the exposed surface.

choices.text: the media player, which decodes untrusted files
choices.why: Once a common route, and much less so now.

choices.text: the browser, which runs code from strangers all day
choices.why: That is what it is for, and what makes it the target.

choices.text: the office suite, which opens the files other people send
choices.why: A real risk, and smaller.

prompt: What happens on the day a device stops receiving updates?

choices.text: the maker disables the features that were risky
choices.why: Nothing is disabled.

choices.text: it stops connecting to the network safely
choices.why: It connects exactly as before.

choices.text: it warns the owner that support has ended
choices.why: Rarely, and never usefully.

choices.text: nothing, and every problem found after it stays open
choices.why: It arrives quietly, which is the difficulty.

prompt: What is the legitimate reason to delay an update?

choices.text: a feature version can break a driver or a program
choices.why: A week is a reasonable wait on a work machine.

choices.text: updates are the usual reason a machine becomes slow
choices.why: A common belief and not true.

choices.text: a security fix often causes more harm than it prevents
choices.why: The lesson says the opposite.

choices.text: the disk may not have room for the download
choices.why: A practical snag, not a reason to wait.

prompt: Which of these are true about updates?

choices.text: feature and security updates can be treated differently
choices.why: The difference is usually stated.

choices.text: a slow machine is usually slow because of updates
choices.why: That belief costs people the cheapest defence.

choices.text: the restart is part of the update
choices.why: Downloaded and not applied is the same as nothing.

choices.text: a phone that no longer updates should not hold codes
choices.why: Every new problem found stays open on it.

prompt: What are the three parts of the shape?

choices.text: a stranger, a story and a small first request
choices.why: Describes some, and not the general shape.

choices.text: an e-mail, an attachment and a demand for money
choices.why: One form of it out of many.

choices.text: urgency, authority, and a channel you did not choose
choices.why: All three together is the shape.

choices.text: a link, a misspelling and a telephone number from abroad
choices.why: Those are tells, and a good imitation has none.

prompt: Why does urgency appear in almost every scam?

choices.text: it explains why the sender is unfamiliar
choices.why: That is what authority is for.

choices.text: it makes the message more likely to be read
choices.why: Being read is not the difficulty.

choices.text: it makes the amount seem smaller than it is
choices.why: Not the mechanism.

choices.text: it removes the step where the person checks
choices.why: Nothing legitimate is harmed by twenty minutes.

prompt: Why is "a channel you did not choose" the useful part?

choices.text: the channel is the only thing that can actually be traced
choices.why: Not what it buys.

choices.text: a legitimate business never makes the first contact itself
choices.why: They do, constantly.

choices.text: an unexpected message is almost always a scam
choices.why: Most are not, and that rule cries wolf.

choices.text: it inverts cleanly: you calling them cannot be faked
choices.why: That is the habit the whole section builds.

prompt: Who legitimately asks for the code that was sent to you?

choices.text: the bank, when it has called you first
choices.why: Especially not then.

choices.text: the platform, when an account is being recovered
choices.why: Recovery does not work that way.

choices.text: nobody, ever, under any circumstances
choices.why: That is the whole point of the code.

choices.text: support staff, to confirm they reached the right person
choices.why: They confirm you another way.

prompt: What is the one habit that defeats the whole category?

choices.text: use a different password for every single site
choices.why: Essential, and it is a different defence.

choices.text: check the spelling of the address it came from
choices.why: A tell, and a good imitation has none.

choices.text: never open attachments from people you do not know
choices.why: Good, and it covers one form.

choices.text: hang up and call back on a number you found
choices.why: A scam cannot survive you leaving the conversation.

prompt: Why has "the grammar is wrong" become unreliable?

choices.text: most messages are now sent by legitimate senders
choices.why: Unrelated.

choices.text: writing a clean message in any language is easy now
choices.why: The tell aged, and the shape did not.

choices.text: scammers have always hired professional writers
choices.why: Not the reason given.

choices.text: people no longer read messages closely enough
choices.why: True and separate.

prompt: Somebody searches for their bank and clicks the first result. What is the risk?

choices.text: a paid result can lead to a copy of the page
choices.why: The address is the only thing that distinguishes them.

choices.text: the page may be an older version of the site
choices.why: Not the risk described.

choices.text: the search engine records which bank they use
choices.why: True, and a different concern.

choices.text: search results are slower than the app is
choices.why: Not a safety matter.

prompt: What protection does an instant transfer remove?

choices.text: time, and with it the ability to dispute
choices.why: A card payment can be argued about for weeks.

choices.text: the need to know the other account details
choices.why: Convenience, not protection.

choices.text: the record of who was paid and when
choices.why: The record is better, not worse.

choices.text: the limit on how much can be sent at once
choices.why: Limits still exist.

prompt: Why is a request from somebody you know the most effective form?

choices.text: messaging apps do not warn about known contacts
choices.why: Not the mechanism.

choices.text: the request arrives when the person is at home
choices.why: Timing is not what makes it work.

choices.text: it skips every suspicion aimed at strangers
choices.why: A cloned account has the photograph and the name.

choices.text: a familiar person can ask for a larger amount
choices.why: They usually ask for a plausible one.

prompt: How do you verify a relative asking for money?

choices.text: call the number you already have for them
choices.why: A cloned account cannot answer the phone.

choices.text: ask a question only the real person could answer
choices.why: Better than nothing, and answerable from their chats.

choices.text: check whether the profile photograph is theirs
choices.why: It is theirs. That is the point.

choices.text: reply asking them to confirm it is really them
choices.why: You are asking the scammer.

prompt: What is the last screen on which a transfer is still yours?

choices.text: the one showing the name of who will be paid
choices.why: A name that does not match the story is the answer.

choices.text: the notification that arrives a moment later
choices.why: Later still.

choices.text: the one confirming the transfer has been sent
choices.why: That is after it has gone.

choices.text: the one asking for the amount to send
choices.why: The name comes after.

prompt: A marketplace seller wants to complete the sale off the platform. Why?

choices.text: the platform's protection is what is being removed
choices.why: That is the entire purpose of the request.

choices.text: the platform does not support instant transfers
choices.why: Most do.

choices.text: the platform charges the seller a fee to use it

choices.text: messages on the platform are slower to arrive
choices.why: Not why.

prompt: Which defences protect a stolen phone's messaging account?

choices.text: the app PIN for re-registering the number

choices.text: a screen lock on the phone
choices.why: A signed-in phone is the account.

choices.text: deleting old conversations regularly

prompt: Why change the password from a different device?

choices.text: a second device proves who you are to the site
